title: Mastering PDR Regression: Clinical Markers & Post-Treatment Assessment
summary: This guide delineates the objective clinical signs of proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) regression following pan-retinal photocoagulation (PRP) or anti-VEGF therapy. Recognizing these markers is vital for preventing sight-threatening complications.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology of Regression
sections.content: Regression in PDR is defined by the involution of neovascularization (NV) following a reduction in intraocular VEGF levels. Mechanistically, this involves the collapse of immature vascular channels, apoptosis of endothelial cells, and replacement of leaky, fragile vessels with fibrous glial tissue (fibrotic transformation).

sections.title: Clinical Signs of Regression
content: Blanching of neovascular fronds (loss of central perfusion)
Reduction in caliber and tortuosity of NVD/NVE
Reduction in associated intraretinal or preretinal hemorrhages
Resolution of hard exudates and lipid deposition
Decreased vascular permeability on Fluorescein Angiography

sections.title: Stages of NV Involution
content: Step 1: Early Response (Days 1-7): Reduction in vessel permeability/leakage.
Step 2: Active Regression (Weeks 2-8): Fragile vessels collapse and lose caliber.
Step 3: Fibrosis (Months 3+): Replacement by acellular fibrous white cords.
Step 4: Stabilization: Maintenance of quiescent state without new NV growth.

rows: Absence of late-phase leakage from previously active NVs.
Demonstration of absent flow signal in neovascular complexes.
Monitoring for tractional retinal detachment despite regression.

sections.title: Red Flags: Non-Regression & Progression
content: Continued leakage on FFA despite full PRP
Iris neovascularization (NVI) or secondary neovascular glaucoma

content.explanation: F: Fibrosis replacing vessels; A: Abatement of leakage; D: Decreased caliber/size; E: Empty/ghost vessels visible on exam.

rows: Stable scar tissue, no leakage on FFA.
Chorioretinal atrophy from laser burns vs. fibrous NV.

sections.title: Landmark Studies & Recent Advances
content: DRCR.net Protocol S: Demonstrated that anti-VEGF (Ranibizumab) is non-inferior to PRP for PDR management.
CLARITY Study: Aflibercept vs. PRP; showed superior regression rates for anti-VEGF in PDR.
OCT-A advancements allow for quantification of vessel density and flow, providing objective metrics for regression beyond clinical observation.
